question: What is the maximum deduction allowed under section 80C of the Income-tax Act, 1961?
expected_answer: Rs 1,50,000 in aggregate for the sums listed in section 80C(2) (old regime).
notes: ita-1961 p.394: 80C(1) '... as does not exceed one hundred and fifty thousand rupees'.

question: My company pays a CA for professional services. At what rate must it deduct TDS under section 194J, and above what amount?
expected_answer: 10% for fees for professional services under section 194J, once the fees paid or credited in the financial year exceed Rs 50,000.
notes: ita-1961 p.816: 'ten per cent of such sum in other cases'; threshold [fifty] thousand rupees, substituted for thirty by Act 7 of 2025 w.e.f. 1-4-2025.

question: Under section 194J of the Income-tax Act, 1961, what is the TDS rate on fees for technical services (not being professional services)?
expected_answer: 2% of the sum for fees for technical services (not professional services); 10% applies in other cases.
notes: ita-1961 p.816: 'two per cent of such sum in case of fees for technical services (not being a professional services)'.

question: What TDS rates apply under section 194C on payments to contractors?
expected_answer: 1% where the contractor is an individual or HUF, and 2% for any other contractor (section 194C(1)).
notes: ita-1961 p.809: 194C(1)(i) one per cent individual/HUF; (ii) two per cent others.

question: When is no TDS required under section 194C on a contract payment?
expected_answer: When a single sum does not exceed Rs 30,000, unless the aggregate paid or credited in the financial year exceeds Rs 1,00,000 (section 194C(5)).
notes: ita-1961 p.809: 194C(5) 'does not exceed thirty thousand rupees' and the aggregate proviso 'exceeds one lakh rupees'.

question: Under section 194-I, what are the TDS rates on rent, and what monthly rent is exempt from deduction?
expected_answer: 2% for plant, machinery or equipment and 10% for land, building or furniture; no deduction where the rent for a month or part of a month does not exceed Rs 50,000 (section 194-I).
notes: ita-1961 p.814: rates (a) two per cent, (b) ten per cent; first proviso: rent per month not exceeding fifty thousand rupees.

question: How much can I claim under section 80D for health insurance premium paid for myself and my family?
expected_answer: Up to Rs 25,000 in aggregate for health insurance (including preventive health check-up) for the assessee and family under section 80D.
notes: ita-1961 p.409: 80D '... as does not exceed in the aggregate twenty-five thousand rupees'. Higher limits apply for senior citizens.

question: What is the extra deduction for NPS contributions under section 80CCD(1B)?
expected_answer: An additional deduction of up to Rs 50,000 for contributions to the notified pension scheme (NPS) under section 80CCD(1B), over and above section 80CCD(1).
notes: ita-1961 p.405: 80CCD(1B) 'which shall not exceed fifty thousand rupees'.

question: Is there a combined cap on deductions under sections 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD(1)?
expected_answer: Yes. Section 80CCE caps the aggregate of deductions under sections 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD(1) at Rs 1,50,000.
notes: ita-1961 p.407: 80CCE 'shall not, in any case, exceed one hundred and fifty thousand rupees'.

question: Under the presumptive taxation scheme of section 44AD, what percentage of turnover is deemed to be profit?
expected_answer: 8% of total turnover or gross receipts, reduced to 6% for amounts received by account payee cheque, bank draft or electronic modes (section 44AD(1)).
notes: ita-1961 p.290: 44AD(1) eight per cent; proviso six per cent for banking/electronic receipts.

question: Up to what turnover can a business use section 44AD presumptive taxation?
expected_answer: Total turnover or gross receipts up to Rs 2 crore, raised to Rs 3 crore where cash receipts do not exceed 5% of turnover (section 44AD).
notes: ita-1961 p.290: Explanation (b)(ii) 'two crore rupees'; proviso 'three crore rupees' when cash receipts do not exceed five per cent.

question: I'm a doctor. What profit is presumed under section 44ADA, and what is the gross receipts limit?
expected_answer: 50% of gross receipts is presumed as profit under section 44ADA, for gross receipts up to Rs 50 lakh, or Rs 75 lakh where cash receipts do not exceed 5%.
notes: ita-1961 p.292: 44ADA(1) fifty per cent; fifty lakh rupees, seventy-five lakh rupees under the proviso.

question: Under section 139(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, what is the return due date for a company or an assessee whose accounts must be audited?
expected_answer: 31st October of the assessment year, or 30th November where a transfer pricing report under section 92E applies (Explanation 2 table to section 139(1)).
notes: ita-1961 p.677: Explanation 2 table (substituted by Act 4 of 2026 w.e.f. 1-3-2026), Sl. No. 2: 30th November / 31st October. The extracted text loses the due-date column for rows 3-4, so those rows are not asked about.

question: When is house rent allowance not exempt under section 10(13A)?
expected_answer: Section 10(13A) does not apply where the residential accommodation occupied by the assessee is owned by him, or where he has not actually incurred expenditure on rent.
notes: ita-1961 section 10(13A), Explanation (a) owned by him, (b) has not actually incurred expenditure on payment of rent. The exempt amount itself is prescribed by rule.

question: Under section 87A, what rebate is available in the new tax regime and up to what income?
expected_answer: For income taxed under section 115BAC(1A), a rebate of 100% of tax or Rs 60,000, whichever is less, where total income does not exceed Rs 12 lakh, with marginal relief just above Rs 12 lakh (section 87A).
notes: ita-1961 p.508: first proviso (a) [twelve] hundred thousand rupees and [sixty] thousand rupees; (b) marginal relief.

question: What standard deduction can a salaried employee claim under section 16?
expected_answer: Rs 50,000 or the salary, whichever is less, under section 16(ia); Rs 75,000 where tax is computed under the new regime of section 115BAC(1A).
notes: ita-1961 p.165: 16(ia) fifty thousand rupees; proviso seventy-five thousand rupees under 115BAC(1A).

question: How does the Income-tax Act, 2025 define a 'tax year'?
expected_answer: Under section 3, the tax year is the twelve-month period of the financial year commencing on 1st April (for a new business or source, from its start to the end of that financial year).
notes: ita-2025 p.24: section 3(1) 'the twelve months period of the financial year commencing on the 1st April'.

question: Under the new tax regime in the Income-tax Act, 2025, what rate applies to income between Rs 12 lakh and Rs 16 lakh?
expected_answer: 15% on total income from Rs 12,00,001 to Rs 16,00,000 under the section 202(1) table.
notes: ita-2025 p.226: section 202(1) Table, Sl. No. 4.

question: What rebate does section 156 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 give a resident individual taxed under the new regime?
expected_answer: 100% of tax or Rs 60,000, whichever is less, where income does not exceed Rs 12 lakh, with marginal relief above Rs 12 lakh (section 156(2)); Rs 12,500 up to Rs 5 lakh otherwise (section 156(1)).
notes: ita-2025 p.186: section 156(1) Rs 12500 / Rs 500000; 156(2)(a) Rs 60000 / twelve lakh rupees; (b) marginal relief.

question: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, what is the TDS rate on fees for professional services and the threshold?
expected_answer: 10% (2% for fees for technical services, certain film royalty and call centres), with a threshold of Rs 50,000, under the section 393 table (serial 6(iii)).
notes: ita-2025 p.398: section 393 Table, Sl. No. 6(iii): Rate (b) 10%; Threshold (i) Rs 50,000.

question: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, by when must a company file its return of income?
expected_answer: 31st October, unless it must furnish a transfer pricing report under section 172, in which case 30th November (section 263(1) Table).
notes: ita-2025 p.290: section 263(1) Table, Sl. No. 2 company 31st October; Sl. No. 1 report under section 172, 30th November; Sl. No. 5 any other assessee 31st July.

question: Above what turnover must a supplier register under the CGST Act?
expected_answer: Aggregate turnover exceeding Rs 20 lakh in a financial year, or Rs 10 lakh for supplies from special category States (section 22(1)).
notes: cgst-act-2017 p.24: section 22(1) 'exceeds twenty lakh rupees'; proviso 'ten lakh rupees'.

question: Who can opt for the composition levy under section 10 of the CGST Act, and at what maximum rates?
expected_answer: A registered person whose aggregate turnover in the preceding year did not exceed Rs 50 lakh (the Government may raise this to up to Rs 1 crore), paying at most 1% of turnover for manufacturers, 2.5% for restaurant supplies and 0.5% for other suppliers.
notes: cgst-act-2017 p.14: section 10(1) as in the corpus copy of the Act (original text; later amendments and notifications raised the limit).

question: What interest is payable under the CGST Act if GST is paid late?
expected_answer: Interest at a notified rate not exceeding 18% for the period the tax remains unpaid (section 50(1)); up to 24% on undue or excess input tax credit claims (section 50(3)).
notes: cgst-act-2017 p.38: section 50(1) 'not exceeding eighteen per cent'; 50(3) 'not exceeding twenty-four per cent'.

question: Within what time must a GST refund application be filed?
expected_answer: Before the expiry of two years from the relevant date (section 54(1) of the CGST Act).
notes: cgst-act-2017 p.41: section 54(1) 'before the expiry of two years from the relevant date'.

question: Which section of the Income-tax Act, 2025 corresponds to section 80C of the 1961 Act (deduction for life insurance premia, PF contributions, etc.)?
expected_answer: Section 123 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (with Schedule XV), which keeps the Rs 1,50,000 limit.
notes: ita-2025 s.123 p.159 'does not exceed Rs 150000'; ita-1961 s.80C p.394. Verified by reading both enacted Acts in the corpus: same subject and the same operative figures. The official CBDT 1961-to-2025 navigator (incometaxindia.gov.in) blocks automated access; check by hand.

question: Which section of the new Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces section 80D (health insurance premia)?
expected_answer: Section 126 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, which allows up to Rs 25,000 for the assessee and family.
notes: ita-2025 s.126 p.161 'up to Rs25000 in aggregate'; ita-1961 s.80D p.409. Verified by reading both enacted Acts in the corpus: same subject and the same operative figures. The official CBDT 1961-to-2025 navigator (incometaxindia.gov.in) blocks automated access; check by hand.

question: Section 80CCD (NPS contributions) of the 1961 Act corresponds to which section of the Income-tax Act, 2025?
expected_answer: Section 124 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (employer and assessee contribution to the pension scheme), including the separate Rs 50,000 deduction that was section 80CCD(1B).
notes: ita-2025 s.124 p.160 sub-section (3) 'not exceeding Rs50000'; ita-1961 s.80CCD p.405. Verified by reading both enacted Acts in the corpus: same subject and the same operative figures. The official CBDT 1961-to-2025 navigator (incometaxindia.gov.in) blocks automated access; check by hand.

question: Where is the section 87A rebate (individuals with income up to Rs 12 lakh) in the Income-tax Act, 2025?
expected_answer: Section 156 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (rebate of income-tax in case of certain individuals).
notes: ita-2025 s.156 p.186 Rs 12500/Rs 500000 and Rs 60000/twelve lakh; ita-1961 s.87A p.508 same figures. Verified by reading both enacted Acts in the corpus: same subject and the same operative figures. The official CBDT 1961-to-2025 navigator (incometaxindia.gov.in) blocks automated access; check by hand.

question: Which section of the Income-tax Act, 2025 contains the new tax regime that was section 115BAC?
expected_answer: Section 202 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (new tax regime for individuals, HUFs and others).
notes: ita-2025 s.202 p.226 slab table 4L/8L/12L/16L/20L/24L; ita-1961 s.115BAC. Verified by reading both enacted Acts in the corpus: same subject and the same operative figures. The official CBDT 1961-to-2025 navigator (incometaxindia.gov.in) blocks automated access; check by hand.

question: Where did the presumptive taxation of section 44AD (8% of turnover) go in the Income-tax Act, 2025?
expected_answer: Section 58 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, whose table keeps 6%/8% of turnover for eligible businesses up to Rs 2 crore (Rs 3 crore with limited cash receipts).
notes: ita-2025 s.58 p.88 Table Sl. No. 1; ita-1961 s.44AD p.290. Verified by reading both enacted Acts in the corpus: same subject and the same operative figures. The official CBDT 1961-to-2025 navigator (incometaxindia.gov.in) blocks automated access; check by hand.

question: Which section of the Income-tax Act, 2025 has the presumptive scheme for professionals that was section 44ADA?
expected_answer: Section 58 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, which presumes 50% of gross receipts for professionals with receipts up to Rs 50 lakh (Rs 75 lakh with limited cash receipts).
notes: ita-2025 s.58 p.88 Table (50% of the gross receipts, seventy-five lakh rupees); ita-1961 s.44ADA p.292. Verified by reading both enacted Acts in the corpus: same subject and the same operative figures. The official CBDT 1961-to-2025 navigator (incometaxindia.gov.in) blocks automated access; check by hand.

question: Section 139 (return of income and due dates) of the 1961 Act maps to which section of the Income-tax Act, 2025?
expected_answer: Section 263 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (return of income), whose table sets the due dates (31st July, 31st October, 30th November).
notes: ita-2025 s.263 p.290; ita-1961 s.139 p.677 (Explanation 2 due dates). Verified by reading both enacted Acts in the corpus: same subject and the same operative figures. The official CBDT 1961-to-2025 navigator (incometaxindia.gov.in) blocks automated access; check by hand.

question: The standard deduction from salary was in section 16 of the 1961 Act. Which section of the Income-tax Act, 2025 provides it?
expected_answer: Section 19 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (deductions from salaries): Rs 75,000 under the new regime of section 202(1), otherwise Rs 50,000.
notes: ita-2025 s.19 p.41 Table Sl. No. 2; ita-1961 s.16(ia) p.165. Verified by reading both enacted Acts in the corpus: same subject and the same operative figures. The official CBDT 1961-to-2025 navigator (incometaxindia.gov.in) blocks automated access; check by hand.

question: Which section of the Income-tax Act, 2025 corresponds to section 80GG (deduction for rent paid without HRA)?
expected_answer: Section 134 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (deductions in respect of rents paid): rent above 10% of total income, up to Rs 5,000 a month or 25% of total income, whichever is less.
notes: ita-2025 s.134 p.170 '10% ... Rs 5000 per month, or 25%'; ita-1961 s.80GG p.425 same figures. Verified by reading both enacted Acts in the corpus: same subject and the same operative figures. The official CBDT 1961-to-2025 navigator (incometaxindia.gov.in) blocks automated access; check by hand.

question: What does CBDT Circular No. 3/2025 deal with?
expected_answer: Deduction of income-tax (TDS) from salaries under section 192 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 during financial year 2024-25.
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-03 p.1 subject line; dated 20 February 2025.

question: As per Circular 3/2025, up to what income is the new-regime tax rate nil for FY 2024-25?
expected_answer: Up to Rs 3,00,000 (FY 2024-25 rates under section 115BAC: nil up to Rs 3,00,000, then 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% and 30% above Rs 15,00,000).
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-03 para 4 table (Finance (No.2) Act, 2024 rates).

question: Per CBDT's salary TDS circular for FY 2024-25, above what income does the 30% new-regime rate apply?
expected_answer: Above Rs 15,00,000 (Circular 3/2025, para 4).
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-03 para 4 table, Sl. No. 6.

question: What section 87A rebate does Circular 3/2025 describe for the new regime in FY 2024-25?
expected_answer: Under the new regime, a rebate of 100% of tax or Rs 25,000, whichever is less, where total income does not exceed Rs 7 lakh, with marginal relief above Rs 7 lakh (Circular 3/2025, para 13).
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-03 para 13 (proviso to 87A inserted by Finance Act, 2023). Note: FY 2025-26 raised this to Rs 60,000 / Rs 12 lakh.

question: What is the leave encashment exemption limit for non-government employees mentioned in Circular 3/2025?
expected_answer: Rs 25,00,000, enhanced by CBDT Notification No. 31/2023 dated 24.05.2023 (section 10(10AA)(ii)).
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-03 para 11.

question: Under the old regime, what surcharge applies to income above Rs 5 crore according to Circular 3/2025?
expected_answer: 37% (excluding dividend income and income under sections 111A, 112 and 112A).
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-03 para 3 surcharge table, (d).

question: How is rent-free unfurnished accommodation owned by a private employer valued in a city with population over 40 lakh, per Circular 3/2025?
expected_answer: At 10% of salary (7.5% in cities with population over 15 lakh up to 40 lakh, 5% elsewhere), as reduced by any rent paid by the employee (Rule 3).
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-03 para 8 table (Income-tax (Eighteenth Amendment) Rules, 2023, w.e.f. 01.09.2023).

question: How does Circular 3/2025 define a 'remote area' for perquisite valuation?
expected_answer: Any area other than one within the local limits of, or within 30 km (aerially) of, a municipality or cantonment board with a population of 1,00,000 or more as per the 2011 census.
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-03 para 9 (Explanation (v) to Rule 3).

question: Can an employee ask the employer to take other income and TDS into account for salary TDS, per Circular 3/2025?
expected_answer: Yes. Under section 192(2B) the employee may give the employer particulars of other income, tax deducted or collected under other provisions, and any loss under 'Income from house property', which the employer takes into account (it cannot reduce salary TDS except for the house property loss and the TDS/TCS).
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-03 para 5.

question: Who can waive interest under section 201(1A)(ii) or 206C(7) according to Circular 5/2025?
expected_answer: The Chief Commissioner of Income-tax (CCIT) or Director General of Income-tax (DGIT), or the Principal Chief Commissioner (PrCCIT) where there is no CCIT or DGIT.
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-05 para 3; dated 28 March 2025.

question: My TDS payment was debited before the due date but reached the government late because of a bank glitch. Can the interest be waived?
expected_answer: Yes. Circular 5/2025 lets the CCIT/DGIT/PrCCIT reduce or waive interest under section 201(1A)(ii)/206C(7) where the payment was initiated and debited on or before the due date but not credited in time because of technical problems beyond the deductor's control.
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-05 paras 2-3.

question: By when must an application for waiver of interest under Circular 5/2025 be made?
expected_answer: Within one year from the end of the financial year for which the interest is charged.
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-05 para 6.

question: Within what time must a waiver application under Circular 5/2025 be decided, and can interest already paid be refunded?
expected_answer: It must be disposed of within six months from the end of the month in which it is received, and interest already paid can be waived and refunded.
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-05 paras 5 and 7.

question: Can interest under section 201(1A)(ii) charged before Circular 5/2025 was issued be waived?
expected_answer: Yes. Circular 8/2025 clarifies that waiver applications can be entertained for interest charged even before Circular 5/2025, subject to the time limit of one year from the end of the financial year for which the interest is charged.
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-08 para 2(iii); dated 1 July 2025.

question: If the interest relates to FY 2023-24, by what date must the waiver application be filed per Circular 8/2025?
expected_answer: By 31 March 2025 (31.03.2025), one year from the end of FY 2023-24.
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-08 para 2(ii) example.

question: Which earlier circular does CBDT Circular 9/2025 modify, and on what subject?
expected_answer: It partially modifies Circular No. 3 of 2023, on the consequences of a PAN becoming inoperative under Rule 114AAA of the Income-tax Rules, 1962.
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-09 subject line; dated 21 July 2025.

question: A deductor paid someone with an inoperative PAN in May 2025. When is there no liability to deduct at the higher section 206AA rate?
expected_answer: For amounts paid or credited from 01.04.2024 to 31.07.2025, if the PAN is made operative (by linking with Aadhaar) on or before 30 September 2025.
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-09 para 3(i).

question: For payments made on or after 1 August 2025 to a person whose PAN is inoperative, how quickly must the PAN become operative to avoid higher TDS?
expected_answer: Within two months from the end of the month in which the amount is paid or credited (Circular 9/2025).
notes: cbdt-circular-2025-09 para 3(ii).

question: What did CBDT Circular 2/2026 extend for the quarter ending 31 December 2025?
expected_answer: The due date for issuing TDS certificates under section 203 (read with rule 31) for that quarter, extended to 31 March 2026.
notes: cbdt-circular-2026-02 para 3; dated 25 March 2026.

question: Why was the TDS certificate deadline for the December 2025 quarter extended?
expected_answer: Because of technical glitches on the e-filing portal that delayed deductors in generating and issuing the certificates (Circular 2/2026).
notes: cbdt-circular-2026-02 para 2.

question: When e-invoicing was first notified in Notification 70/2019-Central Tax, which businesses had to issue e-invoices and from when?
expected_answer: Registered persons with aggregate turnover above Rs 100 crore in a financial year, for supplies to registered persons, from 1 April 2020.
notes: cgst-notif-70-2019-ct: 'exceeds one hundred crore rupees'; in force from 1st April, 2020.

question: What did Notification 13/2020-Central Tax change about e-invoicing?
expected_answer: It superseded Notification 70/2019 and notified registered persons with aggregate turnover above Rs 100 crore (other than those in rule 54(2), (3), (4) and (4A)) to issue e-invoices, from 1 October 2020.
notes: cgst-notif-13-2020-ct paras 1-2; dated 21 March 2020.

question: Which registered persons are left out of the e-invoicing mandate by Notification 13/2020?
expected_answer: Those referred to in sub-rules (2), (3), (4) and (4A) of rule 54 of the CGST Rules (such as insurers, banks and financial institutions, goods transport agencies and passenger transport services).
notes: cgst-notif-13-2020-ct para 1 'other than those referred to in sub-rules (2), (3), (4) and (4A) of rule 54'. The examples are what those sub-rules cover.

question: From when did the e-invoicing threshold drop to Rs 50 crore?
expected_answer: From 1 April 2021: Notification 5/2021-Central Tax lowered the threshold in Notification 13/2020 from Rs 100 crore to Rs 50 crore.
notes: cgst-notif-05-2021-ct; dated 8 March 2021.

question: What e-invoicing threshold applies from 1 August 2023?
expected_answer: Aggregate turnover above Rs 5 crore: Notification 10/2023-Central Tax replaced 'ten crore rupees' with 'five crore rupees' with effect from 1 August 2023.
notes: cgst-notif-10-2023-ct; dated 10 May 2023.

question: My company's GST turnover is Rs 7 crore. Do we have to generate e-invoices now?
expected_answer: Yes. Since 1 August 2023 registered persons with aggregate turnover above Rs 5 crore must issue e-invoices for supplies to registered persons (Notification 13/2020 as amended by 10/2023), unless they fall in the rule 54 exclusions.
notes: cgst-notif-10-2023-ct and cgst-notif-13-2020-ct.

question: Who pays GST on goods transport agency (GTA) services under reverse charge?
expected_answer: The recipient, where it is a factory, a registered society or co-operative society, a GST-registered person, a body corporate, a partnership firm or a casual taxable person in the taxable territory (Notification 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 1).
notes: cgst-notif-13-2017-rate Table Sl. 1 (original notification as published 28 June 2017).

question: Is GST on an advocate's legal services to a company paid by the advocate or the company?
expected_answer: By the company: legal services by an individual advocate or firm of advocates to a business entity are taxed under reverse charge, with the business entity paying (Notification 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 2).
notes: cgst-notif-13-2017-rate Table Sl. 2.

question: Who pays GST on services supplied by a director to the company?
expected_answer: The company or body corporate, under reverse charge (Notification 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 6).
notes: cgst-notif-13-2017-rate Table Sl. 6.

question: Under GST, who pays tax on services of an insurance agent?
expected_answer: The person carrying on insurance business (the insurer), under reverse charge (Notification 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 7).
notes: cgst-notif-13-2017-rate Table Sl. 7.

question: Is GST on sponsorship services paid under reverse charge?
expected_answer: Yes, when sponsorship services are provided to a body corporate or partnership firm, that recipient pays the tax (Notification 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 4).
notes: cgst-notif-13-2017-rate Table Sl. 4.

question: A bank hires a recovery agent. Who pays GST on the recovery agent's services?
expected_answer: The banking company (or financial institution or NBFC), as recipient, under reverse charge (Notification 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 8).
notes: cgst-notif-13-2017-rate Table Sl. 8.

question: Who pays GST when an agriculturist sells unshelled cashew nuts to a registered business?
expected_answer: The registered recipient pays under reverse charge (Notification 4/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 1: cashew nuts, not shelled or peeled, supplied by an agriculturist).
notes: cgst-notif-04-2017-rate Table Sl. 1.

question: On a supply of lottery by a State Government, who pays GST?
expected_answer: The lottery distributor or selling agent, under reverse charge (Notification 4/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 5).
notes: cgst-notif-04-2017-rate Table Sl. 5.

question: Is GST charged on renting a house to someone who lives in it?
expected_answer: No. Renting of residential dwelling for use as residence is exempt (Nil rate) under Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 12.
notes: cgst-notif-12-2017-rate Table Sl. 12 (original notification).

question: Are health care services by a hospital or doctor subject to GST?
expected_answer: No. Health care services by a clinical establishment, an authorised medical practitioner or para-medics are exempt (Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 74).
notes: cgst-notif-12-2017-rate Table Sl. 74.

question: Is there GST on the ticket for a zoo or a museum?
expected_answer: No. Admission to a museum, national park, wildlife sanctuary, tiger reserve or zoo is exempt (Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), entry 79).
notes: cgst-notif-12-2017-rate Table Sl. 79.

question: What central tax rate applies to goods in Schedule IV of Notification 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate)?
expected_answer: 14% central tax (Schedule I 2.5%, II 6%, III 9%, IV 14%, V 1.5% and VI 0.125%).
notes: cgst-notif-01-2017-rate para 1. Central tax only: State tax is levied at the same rate on top.

question: As originally notified in Notification 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), what central tax rate applied to a non-AC restaurant without a liquor licence?
expected_answer: 6% central tax (Heading 9963, entry 7(i)), as originally notified in June 2017.
notes: cgst-notif-11-2017-rate Table Sl. 7(i). The rate was later amended; the corpus copy is the original notification.

question: As originally notified in Notification 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), what central tax rate applied to hotel rooms with a declared tariff of Rs 2,500 to Rs 7,500 a day?
expected_answer: 9% central tax (Heading 9963, entry 7(vi)), as originally notified in June 2017.
notes: cgst-notif-11-2017-rate Table Sl. 7(vi). Later amended; the corpus copy is the original notification.

question: Salary Rs 14 lakh, new regime, FY 2025-26: how much income tax?
expected_answer: Rs 81,900: taxable income Rs 13,25,000 after the Rs 75,000 standard deduction, slab tax Rs 78,750, no rebate, plus 4% cess.
notes: FY 2025-26 rules (Finance Act, 2025); total from compute_tax, which matches the official slab table.

question: My salary is Rs 12.75 lakh a year. Do I pay any tax under the new regime for FY 2025-26?
